laws.rule: Jalisco (including Guadalajara, Puerto Vallarta and Tequila) charges a state lodging tax (impuesto sobre hospedaje) at 5.0% for 2026 on the base set by the state Ley de Hacienda. The state's 2026 revenue law says the municipalities may set up trusts or agreements with the state finance secretariat to receive income from it (Ley de Ingresos del Estado de Jalisco 2026, art. 12). The state's 2026 revenue estimate for this tax is MXN 689,035,060 (about A$52 million at A$1 = about MXN 13.23).

Jalisco bans selling alcohol to anyone under 18 (Ley para Regular la Venta y el Consumo de Bebidas Alcohólicas, art. 2). Selling and drinking alcohol on streets, roads, parks and public squares is banned unless a fixed venue authorised by the council operates there (art. 22). The governor and councils can order a temporary sales ban for set days and hours, with at least 72 hours' notice (art. 43). The text held on OJN shows a last reform of 24 October 2015.

Jalisco treats enclosed public places, workplaces, entrances, public transport and places where people gather as 100% smoke-free. Smoking, keeping any tobacco product lit, and using electronic vapour devices (with or without nicotine) are banned there (Ley de Protección contra la Exposición al Humo de Tabaco, art. 12, as reformed 16 July 2022). A venue may offer a smoking area only in the open air, fully separate from smoke-free areas (art. 14). Venue owners share responsibility if they do nothing about someone smoking (art. 15 and 18).

Jalisco's mobility law requires motorbike riders to wear a certified helmet while riding, and the rider must check that each passenger wears one. The passenger count can't exceed the number on the registration card, and headlights and tail lights stay on at all times (Ley de Movilidad, Seguridad Vial y Transporte, art. 213). Text held on OJN, last reform 1 August 2023.
